mina: hi all, Mina here - first week on runtime. I'm building from source inside a conda env and hitting a weird linker error. who should I bother?

dan: welcome! paste the error and how you installed CUDA/toolkit.

mina: error below. I installed `cudatoolkit=11.8` via conda in my env because some deps needed it. Host driver is 525.60.13 (CUDA 12.1).
```
ERROR: /home/mina/code/runtime/BUILD:73:1: Linking of rule '//runtime:serve' failed (Exit 1): gcc failed: error executing command ...
/home/mina/miniconda3/envs/rt/lib/libcudart.so: undefined reference to `cuInit'
/home/mina/miniconda3/envs/rt/lib/libcudart.so: undefined reference to `cuDeviceGetCount'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
INFO: Build completed, 1 target failed.
```

olivia: looks like the linker is finding the conda-provided libcudart first (from cudatoolkit) which often doesn't match the host libcuda/kernel module. Conda's cudatoolkit is for runtime inside PyTorch/TF wheels, not host builds.

dan: yep. quick checks: `ldconfig -p | grep libcudart` and `echo $LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. Also `readlink -f $(which nvcc)` to confirm which toolkit you're using. If conda shows up in LD_LIBRARY_PATH or in /usr/bin path order, it can shadow system libs during link.

mina: `ldconfig -p | grep libcudart` shows both /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcudart.so.12 and /home/mina/miniconda3/envs/rt/lib/libcudart.so (11.8). LD_LIBRARY_PATH was empty, but conda prepends env lib dir to PATH. `which nvcc` -> /usr/local/cuda-12.1/bin/nvcc.

olivia: even with nvcc from system, the linker invocation can pick up conda libs if the conda lib directory is seen earlier. For builds, we recommend removing cudatoolkit from conda env or creating a separate env without cudatoolkit. Two options: 1) uninstall conda's cudatoolkit and rely on system CUDA for build; 2) set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64` and `export BAZEL_LINKOPTS='-L/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64'` before building, plus `bazel clean --expunge`.

dan: small trick if you must keep conda cudatoolkit for python deps: rename the conda libcudart so it can't be picked up during link (e.g., move or suffix the file) and restore after builds. Ugly but works for local dev. Better: use our dev container image which has a consistent toolchain.

mina: tried removing conda cudatoolkit and ran `bazel clean --expunge`  build succeeded past link step. thanks!

devx-bot: DevX tip: For reproducible runtime builds, use the official dev container (gcr.io/redwood-runtime/dev:cuda-12.1-2025-02) or ensure host CUDA toolkit & driver are used for linking (avoid conda cudatoolkit for native builds). If blocked >2h, page #oncall-runtime.

mina: switching to dev container for iteration, will open an onboarding note about conda pitfalls. thanks everyone :raised_hands:
